taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes Manier (2004) concluded no subspecies should be recognized.
fieldMarks: Smooth scales, a single anal scale and a generally white, unpatterned belly; at least half of the underside tail scales are not divided.
Yellowish or cream ground colour with 18-35 black blotches separated by pink or reddish interspaces; tail has 6-17 blotches.
Adults usually 56-76 cm, maximum about 104 cm; rostrum protrudes (used for burrowing).
behavior: Nocturnal; retreats to underground burrows or under rocks by day and burrows deep in winter; active about April-September.
Eats lizards and their eggs, small snakes, small mammals and sometimes birds.
Mates in spring; lays 4-11 eggs June-August, hatching in 2-3 months.
habitat: Deserts, dry prairies, arid river valleys, thornbrush and shrubland; sometimes oak-hackberry woodland.
range: Northern California, southern Idaho, Utah, southeastern Colorado and southwestern Kansas south to central Baja California, Jalisco, San Luis Potosi and Tamaulipas; below sea level to about 1,900 m. Not found in Canada.
